episodes.170746: Clusters of thunderstorms developed around midday in north central Alabama, expanding in coverage and intensifying through the afternoon.  These were pulse-type summertime thunderstorms, with very heavy downpours in a short period of time, leading to ponding of water. One of the thunderstorms produced half dollar sized hail in eastern Limestone County.
episodes.170893: An isolated thunderstorm produced localized wind damage in western Maryland.
episodes.170901: Thunderstorms ahead of a cold front produced numerous instances of gale to storm force winds over area waterways.
episodes.170932: Despite the upper-level high pressure centered over New Mexico, it was still an active monsoon day with plenty of atmospheric moisture leading to scattered thunderstorms throughout the afternoon and evening hours of August 6, 2022. The Calf Canyon burn scar was hit yet again with heavy rainfall which flowed towards Montezuma, rendering roadways in the area impassable.
episodes.170941: A severe thunderstorms with damaging wind gusts estimated to 80 mph, blew the shingles off several houses in southeast Elbert County.  In Denver, a strong thunderstorm produced dime size hail and nearly one inch of rainfall in 20 minutes.
episodes.171159: Heavy thunderstorms moved into eastern Pennsylvania producing locally heavy rainfall. One of the storms produced a lightning strike which struck a person.
episodes.171163: Scattered thunderstorms developed across the Delmarva peninsula producing some isolated heavy rainfall. One storm crossed into Sussex County from Maryland and produced some isolated wind damage in Delmar and another storm produced a lightning strike which struck a house west of Bethany Beach.
episodes.171165: Scattered thunderstorms developed across the Delmarva peninsula resulting in locally heavy rainfall and isolated wind damage.
episodes.171166: Training clusters of thunderstorms developed near the intersection of the sea breeze and an outflow boundary approaching from the south. This resulted in an area of heavy rainfall across northern Ocean, southern Monmouth, and eastern Burlington Counties which produced some locally significant flash flooding. Some isolated wind damage was also reported in northern Ocean County. Another cluster of heavy thunderstorms developed late in the evening in Mercer County and across the river in Bucks County, PA and tracked northeast producing locally heavy rainfall as well.
episodes.171186: Daytime heating and a moist atmosphere led to scattered afternoon and evening thunderstorms, some of which produced locally heavy rain.  An isolated storm produced small hail.
episodes.171251: Multiple locations reported a combination of brief heavy rain, flooding, or debris flows.
episodes.171275: A deep layer of monsoonal moisture pushed northwest and north into California, Sierra, and western Nevada in a southerly upper flow that marked the western margins of an area of strong high-pressure ridging into the Great Basin region.  Thickening mid-level moisture coupled with steep afternoon lapse rates and warmer surface heating initiated deep columns of slow-moving moisture-laden showers and thunderstorms with torrential rains over the 2021 Tamarack burn scar. This resulted in widespread flash flooding and debris flows in Alpine County CA that created a number of impacts. Rainfall rates of 2.22 inches per hour were observed during the peak of the storm in Markleeville, CA which corresponds to at least a 500 year recurrence interval and possibly 1000 year, per NOAA 14 atlas.

Thickening mid-level moisture coupled with steep afternoon lapse rates and warmer surface heating initiated deep columns of slow-moving moisture-laden showers and thunderstorms with torrential rains over the 2021 Tamarack burn scar. episodes.171535: A line of thunderstorms became severe over western portions of Todd County, producing wind gusts near 70 mph.
episodes.171540: A line of strong to severe thunderstorms produced gusty winds across portions of Todd County. Monsoonal moisture, combined with training storms, resulted in flash flooding across southern Mellette and northern Todd Counties. Rainfall amounts of three to four inches were reported. Flash flooding quickly occurred as water ponded in fields. Heavy rain washed gravel off rural roads. The Little White River around the confluence with Cut Meat Creek and Oak Creek rose several feet in an hour.
episodes.172075: Slow moving pulse storms created flash flooding conditions across the region. The storms developed in a very moist, buoyant environment where 2000-3000 J/kg SBCAPE and 1.7-1.9 inch PW values, supported very efficient rainfall rates. Shear profiles were weak from the low levels to 300mb and created a 'pulse-type' behavior.
episodes.172132: Showers developed around and over Oahu as a nearby, albeit weak, surface trough and afternoon heating generated the downpours.  The rain produced ponding on roadways, and small stream and drainage ditch flooding.  No significant property damage or injuries were reported.
episodes.172215: Storms with supercell characteristics at times developed in the heat of the afternoon ahead of a cold front, and continued to expand in coverage through the evening and overnight. Up to tennis ball sized hail was observed near the Faulkton area, along with sporadic thunderstorm wind damage. Localized gusts up to 76 mph were observed at and near the Watertown airport as well. After thunderstorms had largely dissipated, environmental conditions became favorable for additional severe wind gusts of around 60 mph (gravity waves). Overall rainfall totals neared 4 inches in a few spots including 4 miles north of Vivian (3.82 inches) and Summit (3.98 inches). Minor street flooding was reported in Aberdeen.
episodes.172321: Multiple waves of showers and thunderstorms moved across central Kentucky on August 6th and 7th as an exceptionally moist environment promoted the development of precipitation across the region. Precipitable water values approaching 2 inches remained over the area both days, and a lack of significant large-scale forcing kept storm motions fairly slow. As a result, multiple instances of flash flooding were observed across the area in locations where thunderstorms lingered for several hours. Additionally, while effective shear was weak, there was sufficient instability (around 2000 J/kg mixed-layer CAPE on average) for isolated severe convection. On August 6th, quarter-size hail was observed in Edmonson County near a maximum in mid-level lapse rates, while isolated wind damage reports were observed on both the 6th and the 7th.
episodes.172370: During the afternoon and evening hours of August 6th, showers and thunderstorms developed across southern Indiana in the presence of sufficient instability. Ample moisture was present across the region, with surface dewpoints in the low-to-mid 70s and precipitable water values approaching 2 inches. The scattered clusters of showers and thunderstorms which developed moved very slowly thanks to weak steering flow and cell propagation was largely driven by cold pool motion and colliding outflow boundaries. One particularly heavy cell was able to sustain itself long enough to produce flash flooding over portions of Floyd County.
episodes.172574: A few afternoon thunderstorms, typical for the summertime, produced a few isolated wind gusts that blew down some trees. Locally heavy rain caused flooding on the south side of Chattanooga.
episodes.173056: Slow moving showers and thunderstorms produced locally heavy rainfall during the morning hours.
episodes.173057: Slow moving showers and thunderstorms produced locally heavy rainfall during the morning hours.
episodes.173135: High pressure was centered off the Mid-Atlantic coast, allowing an upper level disturbance to cross our region. This disturbance combined with daytime heating spawned the development of showers and storms. A couple of these storms grew to severe levels and produced damaging wind gusts. Lightning also caused damaged to two homes.
episodes.173209: Scattered Thunderstorms developed in the evening across portions of Nebraska and South Dakota and continued into the overnight. Thunderstorms stretched from the Nebraska Panhandle, through the northwest and northern Sandhills, into southern South Dakota.
episodes.173245: Heavy rain fell from a thunderstorm causing extensive nuisance street and parking lot flooding in the Idaho Falls area.   Generally 0.70 to just over an inch of rain fell in the 4 to 5 pm MDT period causing the flooding.
episodes.173402: Storms moved southward across southern Missouri producing heavy rainfall and damaging winds. Flooding occurred on several low water areas.
episodes.173420: Storms moved southward across southern Missouri producing heavy rainfall and damaging winds. Flooding occurred on several low water areas.
episodes.173475: An isolated severe storm produced wind damage.
episodes.173495: With a high pressure center sitting east of the state, Kentucky, along with much of the Deep South found themselves in a strong return flow pattern. This consisted of S to SW winds which were able to pump in ample moisture and warm air from the Gulf of Mexico. However, with no boundaries or airmass changes nearby, the flow aloft was not very strong. High moisture and weak flow materialized into slow moving showers and thunderstorms throughout the day on Saturday. As locations saw rain persist throughout the day, isolated instances of flooding and flash flooding were reported across portions of Rockcastle, Powell, Laurel, Jackson, and Estill Counties.
episodes.173497: The thermal ridge continued to keep much of the central CONUS hot in early August, and on the evening of August 6th a front sunk south into northern Iowa. This provided the impetus for convective development that for the most part remained sub severe other than a gust in Kossuth County. After the initial cluster of thunderstorms passed, additional storms developed along the front and trained across northern Iowa overnight. This resulted in a pocket of heavy rain with over six inches reported in a few locations. Despite the heavy rain, no flash flooding was reported, due at least in part to ongoing drought in the area.
episodes.173529: Scattered thunderstorms associated with a surface trough produced heavy rain which caused flash flooding across portions of central and south central Virginia.
episodes.173544: Typical afternoon and evening summertime thunderstorms developed on August 6th and August 9th.  Some of the storms were locally strong, producing isolated wind damage across Central Alabama.
episodes.173557: A line of severe thunderstorms moved from west to east across southeastern North Dakota and west central Minnesota, bringing hail and severe wind gusts.
episodes.173558: A line of severe thunderstorms moved from west to east across southeastern North Dakota and west central Minnesota, bringing hail and severe wind gusts.
episodes.173658: Multiple thunderstorms and storm clusters developed over the North Carolina Piedmont during the late afternoon and evening. A couple of the storms produced brief damaging wind gusts.
episodes.173774: Deep tropical moisture moving west along the southern periphery of strong surface high pressure along the northern Gulf Coast in combination with an upper level low pressure system just east of the southeastern United States enhanced shower and thunderstorm coverage throughout the Florida Keys.  Isolated gale-force wind gusts occurred in association with the stronger thunderstorms.
episodes.173837: Scattered to numerous showers and thunderstorms developed across Middle Tennessee during the afternoon hours on August 6. One storm produced wind damage in Davidson County.
